entries.title: Do sunflowers turn to follow the Sun?
entries.answer: A young sunflower may face east in the morning and turn westward by late afternoon. One side of its stem grows faster than the other at different times, bending the plant as it grows. The movement follows a daily rhythm. Once the stem grows more slowly and the flower head matures, the head often stays facing east rather than turning all day. Early sunlight can warm the head, giving it a head start when insects begin visiting after sunrise.
facts: Researchers have found that more pollinating insects can visit warmer, east-facing mature sunflower heads.

entries.title: How big can a giant sequoia get?
entries.answer: A giant sequoia builds a trunk wide enough to make people standing beside it look tiny. It is famous for the amount of wood in that trunk. The General Sherman Tree is the largest known living single-stem tree by trunk volume. A few other kinds of trees grow taller, but they do not have trunks with as much wood. Wild giant sequoias grow in groves on the western side of California’s Sierra Nevada. Their seeds are much smaller than the huge trees they can become.
facts: The General Sherman Tree is a giant sequoia in Sequoia National Park.

entries.title: How can moss grow without true roots?
entries.answer: Mosses are small plants that often make soft green mats. Instead of true roots, many have tiny threads that hold the plant in place. Moisture can reach much of a moss plant right through the outside. You may find moss where the ground or a rock stays damp, though some kinds can dry out and start growing again when wet. Moss can spread using spores. These may leave a little case that stands above the green mat.
facts: A moss can grow a spore case at the tip of a slender stalk.

What flat or crusty growth on a rock might be a lichen instead of moss?

entries.title: How do evergreen trees stay green all year?
entries.answer: Evergreen plants keep some green leaves throughout the year. That does not mean that each leaf lasts forever. An evergreen tree can shed older leaves as it grows replacements, rather than dropping most leaves at once. Many pines and spruces have narrow needles with a coating that helps limit water loss. Some other evergreens have wide, flat leaves. The trick is keeping living leaves through winter or a dry season, whatever shape those leaves happen to be.
facts: Some plants with broad, flat leaves are evergreen too.

entries.title: How do leaves help a plant grow?
entries.answer: Leaves give many plants a wide surface to catch sunlight. A green leaf uses light, water and a gas from the air to make sugars. That process is called photosynthesis. The lines you see on many leaves are veins. They bring water in and help move sugars where the plant can use them. Leaves also have tiny openings, often on the lower side. Gases and water vapor can move through those openings even when the leaf looks still.
facts: Some plants have leaves divided into little parts called leaflets.

How can water leave a plant through its leaves?
Why do some leaves turn yellow before they fall?

entries.title: How do seeds get far from the parent plant?
entries.answer: A seed often has a better chance to find space and light if it lands away from its parent. A dandelion makes tiny dry fruits that float in the breeze on little parachutes. A burr can hitch a ride by hooking onto fur or a sock. Other plants hide seeds inside sweet fruit. An animal can eat the fruit, go somewhere else and leave some seeds behind. Some seeds also travel by floating in water or rolling down a slope.
facts: The little parachute on a dandelion helps the fruit carry its seed in the wind.

What happens if one of the seeds lands in a good place to grow?
How can a plant spread nearby without moving seeds?

entries.title: How does a pitcher plant catch insects?
entries.answer: Some pitcher plants make hollow leaves shaped like deep cups. An insect can slip inside and find it hard to climb out. The plant gains nutrients as the captured food breaks down. In a purple pitcher plant, rain can collect in the leaf and tiny living things may help break down the material inside. This can help a plant in a wet place where its roots cannot find a large supply of certain nutrients. The pitcher is a special kind of leaf.
facts: Some pitcher plants have leaves that collect rainwater.

entries.title: How does a plant send sugar to its roots?
entries.answer: A leaf might make more sugar than it needs right away. The plant can send some of that sugar to other places through a tissue called phloem. A growing root or fruit might use the sugar, or a plant part might store it. The direction depends on where sugars are ready to move and where they are needed. Later, sugar released from a storage part can travel to a new shoot, even before that shoot has many leaves.
facts: Growing roots and fruits can receive sugars through phloem.

entries.title: How does a plant spread by underground stems?
entries.answer: A rhizome is a stem that grows sideways, often just below the ground. Roots can grow down from it. New leafy shoots can grow up at points along the stem. That is one way irises fill more space over time. The old and new shoots can stay connected through the rhizome even when only their tops are visible. A rhizome can also store food, giving a new shoot a supply before it grows enough leaves to make its own.
facts: The part of a ginger plant sold as “ginger root” is actually a rhizome.

entries.title: How does a root know which way is down?
entries.answer: A root does not need to see the ground to grow down into it. Certain cells near many root tips can detect the direction of gravity. Signals from those cells affect how much parts of the root grow. If a seed is turned sideways, a new root can soon curve downward. Stems often respond by bending upward. The growth pattern is called gravitropism. It helps a seed get some roots into the ground and some shoots toward open space where leaves can catch light.
facts: Shoots and many roots can respond in opposite directions to gravity.

How does growing down give a root a better chance to find water?

entries.title: How does a saguaro cactus keep water inside?
entries.answer: Look at a saguaro and you can see long folds down its green stem. They let the stem swell when the cactus takes in water and draw in as it uses that stored water. Roots that spread out near the surface can pick up some water after a rain. The stem handles jobs that leaves do in many other plants, including making food with the help of sunlight.
facts: A saguaro grows in the Sonoran Desert, in parts of the southwestern United States and Mexico.

entries.title: How does a saguaro cactus save water?
entries.answer: A saguaro has a tall, green stem with folds along its sides. It can store water in that stem when rain is available. As more water enters, the folds unfold some, so the stem can get thicker. Many roots stretch sideways just below the surface, where some rain can quickly reach them. A slow-growing saguaro can live through dry stretches using water already inside. Its sharp spines are different from the wide, thin leaves you might see on a garden plant.
facts: Saguaros grow naturally in the Sonoran Desert and nearby areas.

What jobs can a green stem do in a cactus that has no broad leaves?

entries.title: How does a seed wake up and grow?
entries.answer: A dry seed can hold a tiny plant and its food supply for a long time. When conditions fit what that kind of plant needs, the seed takes in water and swells. A little root often breaks through the seed coat first. A shoot can then grow in another direction and reach the light. Early on, the young plant uses food stored in the seed. After green leaves open, the plant can make more of its own sugar.
facts: For many kinds of seeds, the root begins growing before the shoot.

questions.text: What is hidden inside a seed before it sprouts?
How does a new root keep the seedling supplied with water?
What changes once a young plant has green leaves?

entries.title: How does a strawberry plant make a runner?
entries.answer: A strawberry plant can stretch a long, thin stem across the soil. The stem is called a runner. At places along it, a little copy of the plant can grow leaves and reach down with new roots. At first the tiny plant is joined to the older one. Once its roots and leaves can do enough work, it can survive on its own. This lets one strawberry plant make several nearby plants even in a season when it makes few seeds.
facts: A stem that runs along the ground to make new plants can also be called a stolon.

entries.title: How does a Venus flytrap catch a fly?
entries.answer: A Venus flytrap has hinged leaves with tiny hairs on their inside surfaces. When a small insect moves around and brushes the right hairs within a short time, a leaf can snap closed. The plant can get helpful nutrients from the trapped animal. It lives in places where some nutrients are hard to get from the ground. Its green parts still use sunlight to make sugars, as the leaves of other green plants do. Catching animals helps the plant meet a different need.
facts: Wild Venus flytraps are native to a small part of North and South Carolina.

Where does a flytrap get much of the energy it uses?
How do most plants get minerals from soil?

entries.title: How does water reach the top of a tree?
entries.answer: When water leaves a tree’s leaves as vapor, it helps pull more water upward. Water molecules tend to cling to one another. This lets the pull travel down columns of water inside tiny tubes. The tubes are part of a water-carrying tissue called xylem. Water from the soil enters the roots and helps refill those columns. The whole path can reach from the fine tips of roots to leaves at the very top of a tree.
facts: Water can travel through a path of connected xylem cells.

entries.title: How plants make their own food
entries.answer: A green plant uses sunlight, water, and a gas called carbon dioxide to make sugar. This is photosynthesis. In many plants most of the work happens in the leaves. A green material called chlorophyll helps catch energy from light. With that energy, the plant makes sugars it can use to grow or store for later. During this process the plant also gives off oxygen. The water usually comes from the soil, and the carbon dioxide enters the plant from the air.
facts: Chlorophyll helps give many leaves their green color.
Many algae use light to make sugars too.

questions.text: How do tiny algae help a reef coral get food?

entries.title: How pollen travels from flower to flower
entries.answer: Flowers can make tiny grains called pollen. For many flowers to make seeds, pollen must reach a part of a flower that can receive it. Moving pollen there is called pollination. A bee that visits a flower for food can pick up pollen on its body. On the next flower, some grains can rub off. Some plants use wind to move pollen instead. Plants often need a match between the kind of pollen and the kind of flower, so pollen landing anywhere is only one step in making seeds.
facts: Wind can carry pollen from some kinds of plants.
Bees are not the only animals that can carry pollen.

questions.text: What can grow after a flower makes a seed?
Can a bat visit flowers and carry pollen?
How does the plant get the energy it needs to grow flowers?

entries.title: How seeds start new plants
entries.answer: A seed holds the beginnings of a new plant. A coat helps protect the tiny plant inside. Many seeds also hold food that the young plant can use before it has leaves. With the right conditions, a seed can start to grow. Some seeds are carried by the wind. Others hitch a ride on an animal’s fur or travel inside a fruit that an animal eats. When a seed ends up far from its parent, the new plant may get more light or space to grow.
facts: Some seeds can travel by water.
Germination is the beginning of a seed’s growth.

entries.title: What are pine cones for?
entries.answer: Pine trees make cones as part of making seeds. Small pollen cones release pollen into the air. A larger seed cone has scales, the stiff plates you can see on a pine cone. Seeds grow where they are protected by those scales. In some species, a cone opens when it dries, and the seeds can fall or blow away. A pine tree does not make a fruit around its seeds, which is one way it differs from a tomato plant.
facts: A pine has small pollen cones as well as larger seed cones.

questions.text: How does pollen travel even when a plant has no petals?
How can a small cone come from a gigantic tree?
How do flowering plants cover their seeds differently?

entries.title: What are the eyes on a potato?
entries.answer: The eyes on a potato are places where buds can grow. Each bud can start a shoot if the potato has suitable conditions. A potato is a tuber, a thick storage part that develops on an underground stem. It holds food the plant made earlier. Because it is a stem part, a potato can make new shoots at several points. The thick part of a sweet potato may look similar from the outside, but it is a storage root.
facts: A sweet potato and a regular potato store food in different parts of the plant.

How does a tulip store food in a different way?

entries.title: What can grow from a white oak acorn?
entries.answer: A white oak grows acorns, the hard nuts found under the tree. Much of an acorn gives food and protection to its seed while it waits. Some animals eat acorns right away. Squirrels and jays can also carry them to save for later. An acorn that stays hidden in damp ground may send down a root and grow into a young oak. The acorn’s food can help that plant before it has a crown of leaves to catch much light.
facts: White oak acorns usually begin sending out a root soon after they fall if conditions are suitable.

How does wind move a seed from a different kind of tree?

entries.title: What do plant roots do?
entries.answer: A plant’s roots reach into soil or another place where the plant grows. They help hold the plant steady when wind pushes on the leaves. Many roots also soak up water and minerals. The plant moves those supplies to other parts, including new shoots. A carrot has a thick main root that stores food. Grass often has a spreading bunch of thinner roots. A plant can have important parts below the ground even when you only see leaves above it.
facts: Many roots have tiny root hairs that help take in water.

Is an underground potato a root or a stem?

entries.title: What is hidden inside a tulip bulb?
entries.answer: A tulip bulb packs together a short stem, a new bud and thick layers that hold food. Most of this rests underground when the plant has no green top. When conditions are right, a shoot can rise and use that stored food. Roots can grow from the small hard base. An onion is another kind of bulb. Its fleshy rings are easier to see than the tightly packed layers of a tulip bulb, but their storage job is much the same.
facts: An onion’s thick layers are mostly storage leaves.

entries.title: What is inside a flower?
entries.answer: Colorful petals are the most obvious parts of many flowers. Look closer and you may see small structures that make pollen or collect it. In many flowers, the pollen makers are called stamens. A sticky surface called a stigma can catch grains of pollen. Below it, part of the flower can grow into a fruit with seeds. Some kinds of flowers have all these parts together. Other kinds put pollen-making and seed-making parts in different flowers.
facts: The stamens are the pollen-making parts of many flowers.

entries.title: Why are coast redwoods famous?
entries.answer: Coast redwoods are the tallest living trees known. They grow naturally along a narrow stretch of the Pacific coast in California and a small part of Oregon. Winter rain and summer fog help keep their forests moist. A redwood may rise far above the plants at its foot, yet its cones are fairly small. A redwood’s height tells you one thing about its size. A giant sequoia’s wider trunk often contains more wood even when the giant sequoia is shorter.
facts: Coast redwood and giant sequoia are two different kinds of trees.

What does it mean for a tree to be evergreen?

entries.title: Why do cattails have brown heads that turn fluffy?
entries.answer: A cattail’s tall brown head holds many tiny fruits that carry seeds. When the head breaks apart, they can drift off with a tuft of fine hairs. The hairs help the pieces catch air so wind can move them away from the parent plant. If a seed reaches wet ground with the right conditions, it can sprout. Cattails can also grow new shoots from spreading stems below the ground.
facts: A stand of cattails can spread both by sending seeds away and by growing new shoots close by.

What is a stem that grows sideways under the ground?

entries.title: Why do leaves change color in fall?
entries.answer: A summer maple leaf looks green because it has a lot of a substance called chlorophyll. In fall, as days get shorter, the leaf makes less chlorophyll and the green color fades. Other colors that were harder to see can now show through. They include some yellow and orange colors. Some leaves make additional red or purple coloring in fall. Different kinds of trees can turn different colors, and light and temperature can help change how bright the colors look.
facts: Yellow or orange colors can already be present before a green leaf changes color.

How can a tree move some sugars away from a leaf?

entries.title: Why do little maple “helicopters” spin?
entries.answer: Many maples have dry fruits with a thin wing around or beside a pocket holding a seed. When a fruit falls, the wing can make it turn in the air. The turning slows its trip to the ground. A breeze gets more time to push it sideways, so the seed may land farther from the parent tree. Two fruits often start joined in a pair before they separate. The little “helicopter” you find already carries everything enclosed with that seed.
facts: A winged maple fruit is called a samara.

How can a seed grow after it settles on the ground?

entries.title: Why do plants have stems?
entries.answer: A stem holds plant parts in places where they can do their jobs. A tall stem can lift leaves toward the light. It can also raise flowers where insects or wind can reach them. Inside many stems, tiny passageways carry water and sugars. Stems can be soft, like the stem of a bean plant, or hard and woody, like a tree trunk. Some run sideways instead of growing up. Others are hidden underground and store food.
facts: A tree trunk is a type of stem.

entries.title: Why do plants release water vapor?
entries.answer: Water from damp cells inside a leaf can turn into vapor. That vapor escapes through small openings called stomata. The process is called transpiration. Humid air already holds a lot of water vapor, so the loss is often slower in humid air than in dry air. A steady loss of water through leaves helps move more water up through the plant. If water is scarce, closing the openings can slow the loss and help the plant hold on to water.
facts: Plants can change how wide their stomata open.

entries.title: Why do shoots sometimes bend toward a window?
entries.answer: A young stem beside a window can bend as it grows. The side away from the strongest light can stretch more than the lit side. With one side getting longer, the whole stem curves toward the window. Bending as it grows can put its leaves where they catch more light. Scientists call this response phototropism. Growth can change again if the main source of light moves. The shoot does not turn by moving a joint in the way you turn an elbow.
facts: The same amount of light from different directions can change how a shoot bends.

entries.title: Why do some ferns have dots under their leaves?
entries.answer: Turn over a mature leaf on some ferns and you may see rows of round brown spots. The spots are groups of tiny cases that hold spores. When spores are ready, those cases release them, and air can carry them away. In a suitable place, a spore can start a small separate stage of the fern’s life. Later a new leafy fern can grow. Ferns have roots, stems and leaves, yet they make no flowers or seeds.
facts: A fern leaf is also called a frond.

entries.title: Why do some orchid flowers have surprising shapes?
entries.answer: Some orchid flowers have a broad part that gives an insect a place to land. Other parts can point into a space the visitor must pass through. An insect may brush against the flower and leave with a packet of pollen stuck to its body. When it visits a second flower of the same kind, the packet can touch the right surface. Different orchids use different shapes, smells or colors to attract visitors, and not every orchid depends on the same kind of animal.
facts: Some orchids stick a packet of pollen onto a visiting insect.

entries.title: Why do water drops roll off a lotus leaf?
entries.answer: A lotus leaf can look smooth from a distance. Up close, its surface has tiny bumps and a waxy coating. A drop of water touches only a small part of that surface, so it often rests as a round bead rather than spreading out like a puddle. As a drop rolls, it can pick up loose dirt. The shape of the leaf’s surface and the way water pulls on itself both help explain why a lotus leaf can stay cleaner after rain.
facts: A rolling drop can carry particles of dust away from a lotus leaf.

entries.title: Why is a tomato a fruit?
entries.answer: In a tomato flower, a small part where seeds can develop, called the ovary grows into the tomato. That makes a tomato a fruit in botany, the study of plants. It has seeds inside, just as a peach or a grape does. A cucumber and a pea pod count as fruits for the same reason. People who cook often group these foods with vegetables because of how they taste and how we use them. Both groupings can be useful.
facts: Peas grow inside pods, which are fruits in botany.

entries.title: Why is bamboo a grass when it looks like a tree?
entries.answer: Bamboo can grow tall, hard stems that look almost like small tree trunks. It is still in the grass family, along with lawn grass, wheat and rice. Many bamboo stems have hollow places between solid or stronger joints. A bamboo patch can put up shoots from stems that spread below ground. The hard stalks can be useful as building material in some designs. Their strength and size help explain why a big stand of bamboo can look more like woods than a lawn.
facts: Many bamboo stems have hard rings around places where leaves or branches grow.
